# FDG8088

> DO make the `(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context)` serialization constructor `protected` (`private` for sealed types) when implementing `ISerializable`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.10 Serialization.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8088
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Make the serialization constructor of '{0}' {1}

FDG8088 reports the constructor taking (SerializationInfo, StreamingContext) of a class or struct that implements ISerializable, directly or through a base class such as Exception, when it is not protected in an unsealed class or private in a sealed class or a struct. Legacy serialization is obsolete on .NET 8 and later (SYSLIB0051), where the constructor is not needed at all. Changing the accessibility of a public or protected constructor changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
[Serializable]
public class Person : ISerializable {
  protected Person(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext context) {
    ...
  }
}
```
